Review round 1 completed for selected chapter `1B` only. No score or score range assigned.

Filesystem writes were unavailable because the workspace is read-only; the complete ledger continuation and manifest entries are included below for parent persistence.

### New evidence register entries

**E025 — Target-year strategic export-control revision**

- Canonical key: `https://secdiv.gov.pk/press_release/pakistan-notifies-revised-control-lists-under-the-export-control-act-2004#L40-L45|2022 revised nuclear-biological export control lists`
- Source: [Strategic Export Control Division, Ministry of Foreign Affairs](https://secdiv.gov.pk/press_release/pakistan-notifies-revised-control-lists-under-the-export-control-act-2004), 24 June 2022.
- Locator: HTML lines 40–45.
- Claim: Pakistan revised export-control lists for nuclear and biological weapons-related goods, technologies, materials, equipment, and delivery systems. The revision was notified through Gazette S.R.O. 551(I)/2022 dated 12 April 2022, after consultation with relevant ministries.
- Assessment: Formal target-year policy implementation; medium-high confidence for the legal/regulatory act, lower confidence for the government’s claim that it demonstrates effective nonproliferation.
- Attribution: Government-level action occurring immediately after Sharif became prime minister; technical preparation likely inherited, so personal ownership is unresolved.
- Role: Positive/mitigating institutional evidence, with explicit attribution limits.
- Lenses: `1B.4`, `1B.6`, `1B.7`, `1B.9`, `1B.10`.

**E026 — IAEA peer-review evidence on nuclear safety regulation**

- Canonical key: `https://pnra.org/irrs-conclude.html#L2-L11|2022 IAEA IRRS follow-up findings`
- Source: [Pakistan Nuclear Regulatory Authority, IRRS follow-up mission](https://pnra.org/irrs-conclude.html), 9 March 2022.
- Locator: HTML lines 2–11.
- Claim: An IAEA-led follow-up mission with experts from ten countries reviewed Pakistan’s regulatory system in February–March 2022 and reported progress in regulations, inspections, authorizations, emergency preparedness, radiation protection, and environmental monitoring.
- Assessment: High-confidence evidence for the occurrence and reported findings of an international peer review; host-regulator publication creates some reporting dependence.
- Attribution: The mission predates Sharif’s April 2022 accession. It establishes inherited institutional baseline, not Sharif-specific conduct.
- Role: Mitigating/contextual evidence; not ruler credit.
- Lenses: `1B.3`, `1B.7`, `1B.10`.

**E027 — Formal nuclear-governance architecture**

- Canonical key: `https://mofa.gov.pk/arms-control-and-disarmament#L136-L149|NCA PNRA PCENS NISAS governance structure`
- Source: [Pakistan Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Arms Control and Disarmament](https://mofa.gov.pk/arms-control-and-disarmament), accessed 23 July 2026.
- Locator: HTML lines 136–149.
- Claim: The Ministry describes the National Command Authority as chaired by the prime minister; identifies the Strategic Plans Division as its secretariat; describes PNRA as autonomous; notes IAEA-aligned regulatory updates, peer reviews, and specialist training institutions.
- Assessment: Medium confidence for formal institutional descriptions; lower confidence for effectiveness because the source is official self-reporting.
- Attribution: Supports formal authority and institutional baseline, but does not establish Sharif’s personal direction, appointments, or intervention.
- Role: Context and attribution baseline.
- Lenses: `1B.3`, `1B.7`, `1B.10`.

**E028 — October 2022 command-and-control assurances and external reassurance**

- Canonical key: `https://www.dawn.com/news/1715669#L41-L63|October 2022 military nuclear security assurance and US clarification`
- Source: [Dawn, “Army’s top brass reposes full confidence in Pakistan’s robust security of nuclear, strategic assets”](https://www.dawn.com/news/1715669), 18 October 2022.
- Locator: HTML lines 41–63.
- Claim: A corps-commanders conference publicly expressed confidence in Pakistan’s nuclear command-and-control and security arrangements. The report also records subsequent US clarification that it remained confident in Pakistan’s ability to secure nuclear assets.
- Assessment: Medium confidence: Dawn independently reports the statements, but the security claims themselves originate with military and government officials.
- Attribution: Sharif rejected Biden’s remarks through the PMO, but the military assurance was not shown to be personally ordered by him.
- Role: Mixed/mitigating evidence; external reassurance is contrary to an assumption of demonstrably unsafe management, but does not prove safeguards worked.
- Lenses: `1B.2`, `1B.3`, `1B.7`, `1B.8`.

**E029 — Parliamentary nuclear-prestige rhetoric**

- Canonical key: `https://na.gov.pk/en/pressrelease_detail.php?id=4825#L212-L221|27 May 2022 nuclear capability prestige rhetoric`
- Source: [National Assembly of Pakistan](https://na.gov.pk/en/pressrelease_detail.php?id=4825), 27 May 2022.
- Locator: HTML lines 212–221.
- Claim: The National Assembly speaker described Pakistan’s nuclear capability as a source of pride and “invincible” defense, invoking the 1998 tests and national identity.
- Assessment: High confidence for the speech and date; low confidence for broader policy implications.
- Attribution: The statement was by the speaker, not Sharif. It cannot establish Sharif’s rhetoric or policy.
- Role: Contextual and potentially contrary evidence showing prestige-oriented institutional rhetoric, while avoiding personal attribution.
- Lenses: `1B.2`, `1B.5`.

**E030 — Cyber-risk governance baseline**

- Canonical key: `https://pkcert.gov.pk/uploads/2023/06/2021-National-Cyber-Security-Policy-Final.pdf#L112-L138,L194-L198,L250-L304,L517-L535|National Cyber Security Policy 2021 governance and implementation framework`
- Source: [Pakistan National CERT, National Cyber Security Policy 2021](https://pkcert.gov.pk/uploads/2023/06/2021-National-Cyber-Security-Policy-Final.pdf), accessed 23 July 2026.
- Locator: PDF text sections on ownership and enforcement, Cyber Governance Policy Committee, national incident response, CERT structure, audits, and compliance.
- Claim: Pakistan’s 2021 cyber policy created a governance framework involving central, sectoral, federal, and provincial cyber entities; it also acknowledged weak enforcement and the need for monitoring, audits, and improvement.
- Assessment: Medium-high confidence for the formal policy text; no evidence here of 2022 implementation under Sharif.
- Attribution: Pre-existing policy, not Sharif-owned target-year action.
- Role: Inherited-capacity context and explicit gap evidence.
- Lenses: `1B.7`, `1B.9`.

**E031 — National Security Policy inherited baseline**

- Canonical key: `https://www.nsd.gov.pk/SiteImage/Publication/NSP%20Policy.pdf|National Security Policy 2022–2026 public version`
- Source: [Pakistan National Security Division, National Security Policy 2022–2026](https://www.nsd.gov.pk/SiteImage/Publication/NSP%20Policy.pdf), accessed 23 July 2026.
- Locator: Public policy PDF; direct extraction timed out during this pass. The National Security Division publication listing identifies the 2022–2026 policy.
- Claim: Pakistan’s first public national security policy covered traditional and non-traditional security and was approved/launched before Sharif took office. The public version does not expose the detailed implementation framework.
- Assessment: Gateway/context only because the underlying PDF locator could not be extracted reliably in this pass; exclude from defensible evidence until parent verifies the PDF.
- Attribution: Inherited policy baseline; no Sharif-specific implementation evidence.
- Role: Discovery/context; not final evidence.
- Lenses: `1B.1`, `1B.7`, `1B.9`, `1B.10`.

**E032 — Specialist corroboration of regulatory and training institutions**

- Canonical key: `https://ciss.org.pk/pnra-strengthening-pakistans-nuclear-future/#L137-L142|PNRA safeguards IRRS and NISAS 2022`
- Source: [Center for International Strategic Studies, “PNRA: Strengthening Pakistan’s Nuclear Future”](https://ciss.org.pk/pnra-strengthening-pakistans-nuclear-future/), accessed 23 July 2026.
- Locator: HTML lines 137–142.
- Claim: The specialist article summarizes IAEA safeguards, PNRA physical-protection rules, the 2022 IRRS follow-up, and NISAS’s designation as an IAEA collaborating centre.
- Assessment: Medium-low confidence as an independent source family because it substantially restates PNRA/IAEA-related material.
- Attribution: Institutional and retrospective; no Sharif-specific action.
- Role: Secondary corroboration and mitigating context, not independent proof of ruler conduct.
- Lenses: `1B.3`, `1B.7`, `1B.10`.

**E033 — Cabinet-level public safety assurance**

- Canonical key: `https://www.radio.gov.pk/15-10-2022/pakistans-nuclear-arsenals-in-safe-hands-under-command-control-system-bilawal#L25-L41|15 October 2022 nuclear safety assurance`
- Source: [Radio Pakistan, “Pakistan’s nuclear arsenals in safe hands under command & control system”](https://www.radio.gov.pk/15-10-2022/pakistans-nuclear-arsenals-in-safe-hands-under-command-control-system-bilawal), 15 October 2022.
- Locator: HTML lines 25–41.
- Claim: Foreign Minister Bilawal Bhutto Zardari publicly stated that Pakistan’s nuclear arsenal was secure under a strong command-and-control system and that Pakistan met international standards; he also expressed a preference for continued bilateral engagement.
- Assessment: Medium confidence for the statement; low confidence as independent evidence of actual safety.
- Attribution: Cabinet-level statement during Sharif’s tenure, but not a statement by Sharif and not evidence of implementation.
- Role: Official mitigating rhetoric and diplomacy context.
- Lenses: `1B.2`, `1B.3`, `1B.8`.

### Search and candidate-pool record

Search families used:

- Broad: Pakistan 2022 nuclear policy, command authority, safeguards, strategic-risk governance.
- Primary/institutional: MOFA, SECDIV, PNRA, National Security Division, National Assembly, PKCERT, National Command Authority records.
- Adverse/contrary: nuclear safety concerns, command-and-control criticism, tactical nuclear risks, institutional opacity.
- Dual-use: cyber, biological-weapons export controls, national cyber-security governance, emerging military technologies.
- Local-language: Urdu searches for Sharif, nuclear command authority, export controls, cyber-security and biological risks.

Opened sources produced usable evidence from SECDIV, PNRA, MOFA, Dawn, National Assembly, Radio Pakistan, PKCERT, and CISS. The NDU journal candidate could not be fetched, and the National Security Policy PDF timed out; both remain discovery or gateway candidates rather than defensible evidence.

### Chapter 1B status after continuation

The continuation materially improved:

- target-year formal nuclear/biological export-control implementation;
- independent international peer-review evidence on nuclear safety regulation;
- formal clarification of NCA, PNRA, training, and safeguards institutions;
- contrary and mitigating evidence from US reassurance and cabinet-level statements;
- cyber and dual-use governance baselines.

The central attribution gap remains unresolved. No retrieved source establishes that Sharif personally directed, changed, appointed, corrected, or independently audited Pakistan’s nuclear-risk system in 2022. The strongest target-year act, the export-control revision, was a government/SECDIV process initiated immediately after accession and likely built on inherited work. The nuclear safety peer review predates his tenure. Cyber and national-security policies were largely inherited.

The chapter is therefore saturated for this bounded pass on formal institutional and policy evidence, but not on ruler-specific attribution. Remaining gaps are:

- primary NCA meeting records or decisions;
- Sharif-specific appointments or directives affecting nuclear governance;
- target-year safeguards implementation evidence linked to his office;
- independent findings on nuclear command reliability;
- target-year cyber, biological, or AI-risk implementation and audit outcomes;
- local-language reporting with a precise Sharif-attributable act.
